jobs.title: Business Services Team Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in more than 80 countries and very few roles based in offices.

The company is founder led, profitable and growing. We are hiring a Business Services Team Manager to lead efficient and effective travel, logistics, event, scheduling, expense policy and administration.

This executive role requires outstanding coordination, planning, decision-making, budgeting, procurement, reporting and management. It is a fast-paced and complex operation in the tech industry.

We coordinate large-scale company events which involve travel for hundreds of people from 80+ countries. We run such events four times a year, a significant investment in our ability to shape culture, teamwork, execution plans and strategy. Our team is responsible for travel procurement and logistics, ensuring that these events run efficiently and safely. Visas, travel complications and unexpected situations make this a complex operation to run efficiently, demanding a rigorous approach and high work ethic in the team.

This team also serves as an independent check on expense claim approval, ensuring fairness and consistency across teams and countries. This requires integrity, transparency and accountability, and a willingness to set and politely defend the same expectations of the most senior and most junior colleagues.

Together these responsibilities amount to tens of millions in operational costs and a significant number of tactical and operational decisions.

Our team also provides traditional 'EA' services for company leads, though they do this across departments and as a consistent service rather than as personal assistants; they set and deliver to expectations on specific kinds of work. They schedule meetings, coordinate monthly reports, handle delegated approvals for travel and expenses, work across teams, coordinate with suppliers, and run small projects or initiatives.

Location: Worldwide, home based, except in locations where we have an office, such as London, Taipei and Beijing

Leadership and accountability

This team has a direct impact on every team at Canonical. It is important for them to have excellent judgment and interpersonal skills, the confidence to hold people accountable and defend positions of policy, and the work ethic to move quickly through a large volume of work. It is also essential that the team participate in every company event, from the planning and venue selection stages to scheduling, operations and safety reviews, to ensure that they establish personal relationships with team leaders and can ensure these events run smoothly.

As a manager, your team would be responsible for

  • Travel approvals, logistics and operations
  • Expense review in line with policies
  • Planning of complex company events four times a year
  • Company offices that provide executive briefing and operational facilities
  • Our global duty of care, health and safety programs with comprehensive policies and practices

What we are looking for

  • An exceptional academic track record from both high school and university
  • An undergraduate degree in a technical or business subject
  • Drive, and a track record of going above-and-beyond expectations
  • Leadership and management skills
  • Demonstrable good judgement in matters involving money, policy and in-person interactions
  • Ability to work in a global, multicultural organisation
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, curiosity, flexibility
  • Responsibility, accountability, thoughtfulness and self-awareness
  • Result-oriented, with a personal drive to meet commitments
  • Ability to travel up to four times a year, for company events up to two weeks long

Additional skills that you might also bring

  • Travel industry experience
  • Project management experience
  • Event management and operations experience
  • Business and corporate administration experience

What we offer you

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. jobs.title: Product Manager - Anti Fraud
jobs.jd_full:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

We run a large-scale GPU cloud and AI infrastructure platform. Fraud and abuse — stolen payment cards, fake sign-ups, compute mining, credential abuse, and coordinated free-tier exploitation — directly threaten platform economics, capacity availability for legitimate customers, and our standing with payment providers and cloud partners.

As Product Manager, Anti-Fraud, you own the product roadmap for the systems that detect, prevent, and respond to fraud and abuse across the customer lifecycle — from onboarding and payment through to ongoing consumption. You sit at the intersection of Trust & Safety, Payments/Billing, Risk, Data Science, and Product Engineering, and you balance two goals in constant tension: stop bad actors and keep friction near zero for real customers.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Own the end-to-end anti-fraud product roadmap: signup/KYC checks, payment fraud detection, account takeover protection, and compute-abuse (e.g., crypto mining, resource reselling) prevention.
  • Own the rules and risk-scoring surfaces — the tooling that lets analysts and data scientists define, test, and deploy detection rules and ML models with clear guardrails and audit trails.
  • Own the manual review and case-management experience for the Trust & Safety operations team, including queues, evidence views, and action workflows (block, limit, step-up verification, release).
  • Own customer-facing friction points — verification flows, step-up challenges, and appeals — designed to minimize false positives and protect the legitimate user experience.
  • Identify fraud and abuse incidents early — define the signals, alerts, and thresholds that surface incidents before they scale, and own the detection surface that flags them.
  • Participate in incident reviews and post-mortems, capturing root causes and turning each finding into concrete improvements to detection rules, models, and the roadmap.
  • Ensure timely response to active incidents — drive fast triage, clear ownership, and mitigation, working alongside Trust & Safety, Engineering, and Data Science to contain impact.
  • Write clear PRDs and specs that translate fuzzy risk problems into shippable engineering and data-science work.
  • Partner with Analytics team on detection models — defining the problem, labels, and success criteria, and deciding where rules vs. ML are the right tool.
  • Run experiments and monitor rollouts, watching both fraud-catch metrics and false-positive / customer-friction impact.
  • Work with Legal/Compliance to keep detection and enforcement aligned with payment-network rules, KYC/AML expectations, and data-privacy requirements.
  • Track and report on fraud loss, chargeback rate, false-positive rate, review throughput, and time-to-detection.

We expect you to have:

  • Proven product management experience in fraud, risk, trust & safety, or payments.
  • Strong analytical skills — comfortable with data, SQL or equivalent, and reasoning about precision/recall trade-offs and metrics.
  • Ability to make decisions under ambiguity and to balance security, business, and customer-experience priorities.
  • Solid collaboration with engineering and data science; you can hold a technical conversation about signals, features, and model behavior.
  • Exposure to cloud, SaaS, marketplace, fintech, or infrastructure products.
  • Understanding payment fraud, chargebacks, KYC/AML, or device/network signals (fingerprinting, velocity, IP reputation).

It would be an added bonus if you have:

  • Familiarity with ML-based detection systems and their operational lifecycle (drift, retraining, monitoring).
  • Experience with abuse patterns specific to compute or GPU platforms (mining, credential stuffing, free-tier farming).

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

jobs.title: Agile Project Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Avetta is building the largest global community of hiring clients and suppliers that are Ready to Work. Its unified platform streamlines compliance, prequalification, safety and performance benchmarking in a single, integrated experience. Trusted by 360,000 businesses across more than 120 countries, Avetta blends AI-driven insights and human expertise to close risk gaps and strengthen supplier reliability so projects start on time, risks are managed proactively and operations scale with certainty.

SUMMARY

Avetta is evolving beyond traditional Agile and SAFe delivery frameworks into an AI-Augmented Product Development Lifecycle (AI-PDLC) a structured pipeline where AI agents assist at every stage, from product discovery through to production release, while humans retain ownership of every key decision.

As an Agile Project Manager (APM) in the AI-PDLC, you are the connective tissue of that pipeline. You don’t just track progress, but you ensure the right human judgment is applied at the right gates, so AI-generated work meets Avetta’s quality bar before it moves forward.

This role is ideal for a mid-level Agile delivery professional who is confident running cross-functional initiatives, comfortable working directly with product and engineering pod teams, and genuinely curious about how AI is reshaping software delivery.

Candidates residing within 30 miles of an Avetta office are required to follow a hybrid work schedule of three days in the office and two days working from home each week. Candidates residing more than 30 miles from an Avetta office may be considered for remote employment.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Pipeline Coordination & Flow Management

    • Own end-to-end delivery flow for one or more initiatives across Avetta’s 5-zone AI-PDLC pipeline — from validated discovery through to production release.

  • Track initiative progress using the 3 Red Box milestone model (pipeline entry → approved spec → production), with cycle time and throughput as primary delivery metrics.

  • Coordinate zone-to-zone handoffs, ensuring the right sign-offs are in place before any AI-generated artifact like spec, task breakdown, or code advances downstream.

  • Facilitate the Spec Agreement gate: the checkpoint where both the Product Manager and Tech Lead confirm intent and approach before AI-assisted coding begins.

  • Maintain the Gate Decision Log in Confluence for each initiative: what was reviewed, what was decided, and what changed: the audit trail proving human judgment drove every step.

  • Flag missing or incomplete dependencies (such as the SDAP coding rulebook) early; no AI coding work moves forward without them.

  • Cross-Pod Dependency Orchestration

  • Coordinate across 3–5 person delivery pods, acting as the integration point for work spanning multiple teams, domains, or codebases.

  • Facilitate cross-pod syncs focused on AI pipeline blockers, spec quality issues, and zone-to-zone handoff readiness, replacing traditional Scrum of Scrums.

  • Own RAID and decision logs at the initiative level, with specific attention to AI pipeline failure modes such as unresolved spec questions and AI output drift.

  • Partner with Scrum Masters to surface and escalate pod-level blockers before they become pipeline bottlenecks.

  • Stakeholder Management & Communication

  • Act as the primary communication point between Product Management, engineering pod leads, Release Management, and senior stakeholders for initiative status, risks, and key decisions.

  • Prepare concise, data-driven updates for monthly C-level reporting, structured around pipeline volume, spec approval rate, and production throughput.

  • Communicate spec quality issues and AI agent output concerns clearly, with proposed mitigations not just escalation.

  • Help PMs set stakeholder expectations around AI-PDLC timelines, which may differ from traditional Agile estimates.

  • Spec Quality & Gate Integrity

  • Apply the Spec Rubric (a pass/fail quality checklist) at the approved-spec gate to ensure no work is greenlighted below the agreed quality standard.

  • Surface and report spec rejection patterns as early-warning signals — high rejection rates predict downstream delivery slowdowns.

  • Ensure Definition of Ready criteria are met before any initiative enters the delivery zone.

  • Track open spec questions across initiatives and ensure they are resolved — not bypassed.

  • Tooling, Metrics & Continuous Improvement

  • Maintain delivery data in Jira, Aha!, and Confluence aligned to the AI-PDLC pipeline; log gate timestamps accurately for cycle time reporting.

  • Build and maintain dashboards tracking key metrics: cycle time, throughput, spec rejection rate, PR review cycles, and human gate hours per initiative.

  • Use AI productivity tools (Glean, Claude, Jira automation/Scriptrunner/Atlassian Intelligence) to reduce manual tracking overhead and surface blockers proactively.

  • Coach pod teams and stakeholders on AI-PDLC process expectations, HITL (Human-in-the-Loop) gate responsibilities, and how to engage productively with AI agents.

  • Champion the principle: “The AI generates artifacts; humans own decisions.”

  • Contribute improvement observations back into the AI-PDLC framework: this is a living system and your insights matter.

IDEAL EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION & TRAINING:

  • Experience

    • 3–5 years in Agile delivery, project management, or program coordination in a SaaS or software environment.

  • Hands-on experience with cross-functional teams (Product, Engineering, QA, Design).

  • Background in organizations undergoing Agile or technology transformation; AI-augmented delivery experience is a strong plus.

  • Agile & AI-PDLC Skills

  • Solid understanding of Agile/Scrum frameworks with ability to adapt ceremonies to AI-augmented team models.

  • Familiarity with Spec-Driven Development (SDD) — understanding that input spec quality directly drives AI output quality.

  • Working knowledge of human-in-the-loop (HITL) gate concepts and the distinction between AI-generated artifacts and human-owned decisions.

  • Tools

  • Proficiency with Jira, Scriptrunner, Confluence, and Aha! for initiative tracking, gate logging, and reporting.

  • Experience with AI productivity tools (Atlassian Intelligence, Glean, Claude, or equivalent).

  • Comfortable with Microsoft Teams and SharePoint for distributed team collaboration.

  • Soft Skills

  • Strong written and verbal communication: able to translate AI pipeline status into clear, business-relevant updates for any audience.

  • High judgment and organizational discipline; able to manage multiple initiative workstreams without losing sight of gate integrity.

  • Collaborative, proactive, and comfortable influencing without direct authority.

  • Change-agent mindset with genuine openness to rapid iteration as the AI-PDLC framework matures.

  • Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field; or equivalent practical experience in Agile delivery or program coordination roles.

  • Certifications (Preferred, Not Required)

  • SAFe and AI fluency credentials (SAFe (SA / SSM / SASM / SPC), AWS AI Practitioner, Google AI Essentials) are weighted above traditional PM certifications (CSM / PSM I–II, CAPM / PMP for this role.

At Allucent™, we are dedicated to helping small-medium biopharmaceutical companies efficiently navigate the complex world of clinical trials to bring life-changing therapies to patients in need across the globe.

Looking to take your project management expertise to the next level? Join us as a Project Manager II (PM II) and lead the delivery of complex clinical trials that make a meaningful impact for patients worldwide. We are seeking a strategic and execution-focused leader with strong experience managing Oncology clinical trials who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.

About the Role

As a Project Manager II, you will lead with impact and drive global clinical trials from study start-up through final delivery. You’ll oversee cross-functional teams, ensuring studies remain on track, on budget, and compliant with GCP and regulatory requirements while serving as the primary point of contact for sponsors, vendors, and internal stakeholders. With a focus on proactive problem-solving, risk mitigation, and operational excellence, you’ll play a critical role in delivering high-quality clinical programs that exceed client expectations.

Your main responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Driving project success by leading cross-functional teams to deliver clinical trials on time, within scope, and on budget.
  • Ensuring excellence and compliance by developing and executing project plans aligned with GCP, SOPs, and regulatory standards.
  • Aligning stakeholders by serving as the primary point of contact for sponsors, vendors, and internal teams.
  • Optimizing vendor performance through strategic selection, management, and oversight.
  • Mitigating risks and control budgets by proactively addressing challenges, scope changes, and resource allocation.
  • Maintaining inspection-ready documentation by leading key meetings and ensuring the Trial Master File and study records are complete.

About You

If you are a results-driven Project Manager II with a proven track record of leading complex clinical trials from start-up to closeout. If you thrive in fast-paced environments, excel at aligning teams and stakeholders, and take pride in delivering projects on time, on budget, and with uncompromising quality then this role is for you.

To be successful, we are looking for the following traits and behaviors:

  • Minimum Bachelor’s degree in life science, healthcare and/or business degree

  • Minimum 6 years of relevant work experience, specifically experience in drug development and/or clinical research

  • Minimum 1 year of project management experience, specifically as a clinical project manager

  • Strong expertise managing the unique operational complexities associated with Oncology programs, including oversight of specialized vendors, timelines, safety considerations, and global study execution.

  • Expert knowledge of ICH-GCP(R2), data and patient privacy practices, and applicable (local) regulatory requirements

  • Demonstrates strong financial acumen, administrative excellence and analytical skills

  • Experience managing all phases of the full-service clinical trial delivery lifecycle (Start-up, Maintenance, Close-out).

Our mission is to help bring new therapies to light. When you work at Allucent, that means rolling up your sleeves and applying your unique skill set, expertise, and knowledge to build partnerships with our clients in their pursuit to develop new, life-improving treatments.

Together we SHINE. Find more information about our values.
